DISEASES

  • A disease can be defined as any disturbance in the internal structure and function of any organ or part of the body, which is usually associated with specific signs and symptoms.

Classification of Diseases on Basis of Time

Acute DiseasesChronic Diseases
They last for a short period of time, cause major effects on health in a short time E.g. Fever, cold, cough, etc.They last for a longer period of time and takes a long time to cause major effects on health E.g. Diabetes, TB (tuberculosis), Elephantiasis, etc.

Communicable and Non-Communicable Diseases

Communicable DiseasesNon-Communicable Diseases
These are diseases which spread from one person to another. They are caused by pathogens E.g. Malaria, AIDS, TB, chicken pox, COVID, etc.These are diseases which do not spread from one person to another. They are caused by deficiency of nutrients or due to some allergy or proliferation of abnormal cells E.g. Diabetes, arthritis, asthma, cancer, etc.

Pathogens Responsible for Diseases

  • Pathogens are disease-causing agents, that are responsible for causing infections and diseases in their hosts, often by entering the body and causing physiological disruptions.

Pathogens include:

Virus:

  • They are small infectious agents that need a host cell to replicate and cause diseases like the common cold, flu, and HIV.
  • In virus, the genetic material is included in a protein envelope known as Capsid.
  • Genetic material in viruses are made up of RNA (retrovirus with single stranded RNA) or DNA (with double stranded DNA).
  • Antibiotics work against the formation of cell wall. Viruses are surrounded by a protective protein coating; they don't have cell walls that can be attacked by antibiotics like bacteria do.

Bacteria:

  • They are single-celled organisms that can reproduce and cause diseases like pneumonia, strep throat, and food poisoning.

Protozoa:

  • They are one-celled organisms that can cause various diseases, including intestinal infections, amoebiasis, giardiasis, toxoplasmosis. There often spread through contaminated water or by insect bites.

Fungus

  • A group of eukaryotic organism that can cause diseases like athlete's foot and yeast infections.

Virus Vs Bacteria

VirusBacteria
Genetic material: DNA/RNA + Protein (capsid)They are prokaryotes, they lack true nucleus and membrane bound organelles. Instead, they have nucleoid and their genetic material is called Genophore (bacterial DNA)
Non-living entityUnicellular and living entity
It needs a host cellIt divides on its own
Parasitic in natureParasitic/Saprophytic in nature
Antibiotics cannot be used to treat viral infectionsAntibiotics can be used to treat bacterial infections
Smaller (20-400nm)Larger (1000nm)

DISEASES

Hepatitis (Type A, B, and C)

  • Affects: Liver.
  • Symptom: Jaundice (mainly affects liver).
  • Hepatitis A: Transmitted through food.
  • Hepatitis B: Sexually transmitted through bodily fluids.
  • Hepatitis C: Transmitted when in contact with infected blood.

India's first indigenous Hepatitis-A vaccine: Havisure

Mumps

  • It is a viral disease that affects the parotid salivary glands (cheek and jaw area).

Flu

  • Caused by: Influenza viruses → Types A, B, and C.
  • Influenza also known as "evil influence of stars".

Common Cold

  • Caused by: Rhinovirus.

Polio

  • Caused by: Poliomyelitis/Polio virus.
  • Polio is totally eradicated from India, as declared in 2014.
  • It affects the nervous system, the nerves in spinal cord or brain stem cells.
  • First polio vaccine was created by: Dr. Jonas Salk.
  • India launched the Pulse Polio Immunisation Programme on October 2, 1995.

Cervical Cancer

  • Caused by: Human Papillomavirus Causes (HPV).
  • It affects the cervix region in women.
  • Detected through: PAP Smear Test.

Chicken Pox

  • Caused by: Varicella Zoster Virus.

Small Pox

  • Caused by: Variola Virus.
  • Vaccine by: Edward Jenner (1796).
  • Eradicated from India in: 1977.

Dengue

  • Caused by: Flavivirus (DENV1-4).
  • Carrier of virus: Aedes Aegypti mosquito (also responsible for Chikungunya).

Rabies

  • Caused by: Lyssavirus.
  • In rabies Central Nervous System (CNS) is affected which leads to hydrophobia.

AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome)

  • Caused by: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus → retrovirus).
  • It is a sexually-transmitted disease.
  • Death: Due to weak immune system.
  • Method of transmission: Sexual contact, blood transfusions, from mother to baby.
  • Test for detection: ELISA Test (Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent Assay).
  • "AIDS DAY" is celebrated on: 1st Dec.

Plague

  • Caused by: Yersinia pestis.
  • Death due to plague known as: Black Death.
  • 1897-1906: 12 Million deaths in India was reported.

Leprosy

  • Caused by: Mycobacterium leprae.
  • Leprosy affects skin and is also known as Hansen's Disease.

Cholera

  • Caused by: Vibrio cholera.
  • It is a water borne disease. Death caused due to cholera is known as "Blue Death".

Bronchitis

  • An inflammation of the lining of the bronchial tubes, which carry air to and from the lungs.
  • Most cases are viral, but bacterial causes include Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. (Note: Bordetella pertussis actually causes whooping cough / pertussis, not ordinary bronchitis.)

TB (Tuberculosis)

  • Caused by: Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
  • Vaccine provided against it: BCG (Bacillus Calmette-Guerin).

Pneumonia

  • Caused by: Streptococcus pneumoniae.

DISEASES

Diphtheria

  • Caused by: Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
  • It affects the respiratory system (mucous membranes of nose and throat).

Diarrhoea

  • Caused by: E. Coli (Escherichia coli).

E. Coli is a gram-negative facultative anaerobic, rod-shaped, coliform bacterium.

Peptic Ulcers

  • Caused by: Helicobacter pylori.

Typhoid

  • Caused by: Salmonella typhi.
  • It affects small intestine (gut).
  • Test to detect Typhoid: Widal Test.

Acne

  • Caused by: Staphylococcus bacteria.

Baldness (Tinea capitis)

  • A fungal infection specifically tinea capitis, also known as scalp ringworm, can cause patchy hair loss.

Athlete's Foot

  • A type of ring worm disease that affects the feet.

Ring Worm

  • A common skin infection that can cause a red, itchy rash.

DISEASES CAUSED BY PARASITIC MITE

Scabies

  • Caused by: Sarcoptes scabiei (a microscopic mite, not a fungus — class Arachnida, order Sarcoptiformes).
  • This mite burrows into the skin, where it lays eggs that hatch into adult mites. The mites cause an itchy rash.

Note: Asthma is a non-communicable chronic respiratory condition (often allergic/immune-mediated); it is not a fungal disease.

DISEASES CAUSED BY PROTOZOA

Malaria

  • Malaria Day: 25th April.
  • Protozoa: Plasmodium.

Cinchona tree is found in Evergreen Forest.

  • Carrier: Female Anopheles mosquito.
  • Treatment: Quinine (found in bark of cinchona tree).

Sleeping Sickness

  • Protozoa: Trypanosoma.
  • Carrier: Tse Tse fly.

Kala Azar

  • Protozoa: Leishmania.
  • Carrier: Sandfly.

GENETIC DISORDERS

SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASES (Viral Infections: HIV-AIDS, Warts; Bacterial Infections: Gonorrhea, Syphilis)

  1. 1. Chromosomes: Disorders in chromosomes.
  • Autosomal Disorders: A genetic disorder that occurs when a gene on a non-sex chromosome is mutated.
  • E.g. Down's syndrome: The person has an extra copy (or partial copy) of chromosome 21 (Trisomy 21) for a total of 47 chromosomes instead of 46; Albinism (the body makes little or no melanin).
  • Sex-Linked Disorders: Disorders that affect the sex chromosomes.
  • E.g. Turner's syndrome: One X chromosome is missing in females (XO); Klinefelter's syndrome: One extra X chromosome is present in males (XXY).

Haemophilia affects the recessive gene located on X chromosome. It is a rare disorder in which the blood does not clot.

The signs:

  • A ruler less muscular body than males their age.
  • Smaller hips and longer legs.
  • Larger breast.
  • Weaker bones.
  • A lower energy level.
  • Smaller penis and testicles.
  • Delay in puberty or go a partial amount.
  • Less facial and body hair following puberty.

DISEASES

  1. 2. Mendelian Disorders: Disorders that may occur mainly by the alteration or mutation in a single gene. E.g. Sickle cell anaemia, Thalassemia, Colour blindness, Haemophilia, etc.

Glaucoma

  • It is a disease that damages the eye's optic nerve leading to vision loss or blindness (usually a genetic disorder).
  • Glaucoma is caused when there is an increase in eye fluid pressure (Trachoma) is another disease in which fluid pressure of eye increases but due to a bacteria called Chlamydia trachomatis).

Pandemic, Epidemic and Endemic

PandemicEpidemicEndemic
Sudden increase in cases across several countries, continents, or the worldSudden increase in cases spreading through a large populationThe diseases that are constantly present in a population or region with relatively low spread

Some Other Diseases

  • Wilson Disease: Wilson disease is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder caused by abnormal copper accumulation in the body particularly involving the brain, liver, and cornea.
  • Mad Hatter Disease: Mad hatter's disease refers to neurological symptoms of mercury poisoning (also responsible for Minamata Disease) over a long period of exposure.
  • Siderosis Disease: It is caused due to excessive deposition of iron in body tissue.
  • Itai Itai: It is caused due to cadmium deposition.
  • Blue Baby Syndrome: It is caused due to nitrate deposition.
  • Patau syndrome, also known as trisomy 13, is a genetic disorder caused by having an extra copy of chromosome 13.
  • Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease is caused by duplication of the peripheral myelin protein-22 (PMP22) gene on chromosome 17.
